pois.name: Mount Everest
pois.summary: Highest peak above sea level on Earth, rising about 8,849 meters on the Nepal–China border in the Himalaya. Its summit marks the top of the planet’s solid surface in conventional elevation surveys.

pois.name: Challenger Deep
pois.summary: Deepest known point in the ocean, in the southern Mariana Trench of the western Pacific. Soundings place the seafloor roughly 10,900 meters below sea level.

pois.name: Grand Canyon
pois.summary: Deep canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, exposing a nearly continuous rock record spanning about two billion years. Steep walls and plateaus make it one of Earth’s most studied continental landforms.

pois.name: Great Barrier Reef
pois.summary: World’s largest coral reef system, stretching along Australia’s northeastern coast. Its reefs and islands host exceptional marine biodiversity across a vast shallow shelf.

sources.name: NASA Earth Observatory — Great Barrier Reef

pois.name: Amazon Basin
pois.summary: Largest tropical rainforest basin on Earth, drained by the Amazon River and its tributaries across northern South America. Dense canopy and river networks shape regional climate and biodiversity.

pois.name: Sahara
pois.summary: Largest hot desert on Earth, spanning much of northern Africa. Sand seas, rocky plateaus, and hyper-arid climate define a vast subtropical dry belt.

pois.name: Mauna Loa
pois.summary: Earth’s largest volcano by volume, a broad shield on the Island of Hawaiʻi built by countless basaltic lava flows. Its summit caldera and rift zones remain volcanically active.

sources.name: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory — Mauna Loa

pois.name: Yellowstone Caldera
pois.summary: Active volcanic caldera and hydrothermal province in the northern Rocky Mountains. Geysers, hot springs, and a restless magma system mark one of Earth’s best-known continental volcanic centers.
